content:
The story states that Mark initially wants to buy a hamburger at the cafeteria, but Lenny offers him a hamburger in exchange for help with math homework. Mark agrees to help Lenny with his homework. Since Lenny promised to "give you a hamburger" as part of the deal, the logical outcome is that after completing the homework, Mark receives the hamburger from Lenny and eats it. There is no indication in the story that Mark still needs to go to the cafeteria (option A), nor does it mention activities like reading in the library (C) or playing on the playground (D). The agreement directly involves Lenny providing the hamburger, so the correct action after helping is consuming the hamburger given by Lenny.

STORY: The little boy Mark always wants to eat a hamburger at lunchtime. When he walks to the school cafeteria to buy a hamburger, his good friend Lenny comes to him and says, "Mark, if you help me answer a few questions on my math homework, I give you a hamburger." So Mark decides to help Lenny with his math homework.
QUESTION: What does Mark do after he helps Lenny finish his math homework?
OPTION-A: Mark continues to go to the cafeteria to buy a hamburger
OPTION-B: Mark eats the hamburger from Lenny
OPTION-C: Mark goes to the library to read
OPTION-D: Mark goes to the playground to play
